en: Udāna 1.9 Jaṭilasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Gayā on Gayā’s Head.
Now at that time, during the cold winter nights in the middle of the frosty season, a large number of matted-hair ascetics were plunging into the water at Gayā,
emerging from it, diving in and out, splashing water over themselves, and offering oblations into the fire:
Now the Blessed One saw those many matted-hair ascetics on cold winter nights during the intervals between the rains, at a time when snow was falling,
in Gayā— some emerging from the water, some submerging, some performing the act of emerging and submerging, some pouring water over themselves, and some offering oblations into the fire:
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
“One does not become pure by water.”
but he in whom truth and Dhamma reside—
he is pure, he is a brahmin.”
